To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) when subjects are exposed to three sources, each presenting a single argument in favor of a persuasive position, their attitude toward that position is less extreme than when subjects are exposed (a) to three sources each presenting three arguments in favor of that position or (b) to a single source presenting three arguments.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of source characteristics in persuasive communication.
the role of source and argument in persuasive communication.
the effects of source and message variables on the processing of persuasive communications and the implications of these processes for persuasion.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the multiple-source effect occurs when subjects are not distracted, and that the multiple-arguments effect occurs when subjects can devote sufficient attention to the arguments.
the multiple source effect is the result of increased message processing, which is the result of the combination of multiple source and multiple message.
multiple sources are persuasive, but that the persuasive advantage associated with multiple sources depends upon the number of arguments that are presented.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the multiple-source effect in persuasion is a result of the increased cognitive processing of message arguments, which is in turn a result of the greater perceived importance and relevance of the message arguments when presented by more sources and/or more arguments.
the more sources and arguments, the more persuasion. However, the effect of the number of sources is not as strong as that of the number of arguments.
when the number of arguments presented in the message is held constant, multiple-source messages are more persuasive than single source messages.
The main takeaway from our work is that
when we are exposed to multiple sources of persuasion, the more we think about the arguments the more likely we are to be influenced.
the number of arguments and number of sources are not the only factors that affect persuasion.
people who are exposed to multiple sources and multiple arguments are more likely to be persuaded by the information presented to them.
